top.title: Why Yoro’s red card against Liverpool was overturned – FA panel
top.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye The Football Association has released the written reasons for overturning Leny Yoro’s red card for Manchester United against Liverpool, despite refereeing body Pro Ref maintaining that the on-field decision was not clearly wrong. According to Sky Sports, the FA’s independent regulatory commission unanimously ruled that referee Sam Barrott made an “obvious error” in deciding Liverpool striker Alexander Isak had an obvious goalscoring opportunity when Yoro fouled him during United’s 4-0 defeat at Anfield on Sunday. The panel said Isak’s touch was so heavy that he had lost control of the ball, allowing United goalkeeper Senne Lammens to close in and potentially gather it before the striker could shoot. “Taking the foul committed by Yoro out of the scenario, Isak would not have had an obvious goalscoring opportunity,” the commission said in its written reasons. The decision overturned Yoro’s one-match suspension, making the defender available for United’s Premier League match against Brentford on Saturday. Pro Ref chief refereeing officer Howard Webb had defended the officials’ decision, saying Isak was moving quickly towards the ball and that it was “certainly not clearly wrong” to judge he would reach it before Lammens. United submitted video evidence from several angles, as well as footage of Brighton defender Pascal Struijk’s red card against Sunderland, which was overturned after an appeal. The club also argued that Isak would have been at least 1.8 metres short of the ball without Yoro’s challenge. The commission said it could not test the validity of United’s distance analysis and therefore viewed it with caution. A separate Premier League Key Match Incidents panel is reported to have backed the original decision; its findings for the matchweek are due to be published on December 2. top.title: M.Inc PR Joins Industry Stakeholders to Explore Africa’s Credit Economy at ACE 2026
top.description: A cross section of industry leaders and stakeholders during the fourth edition of Africa Credit Expo 2026 held on Friday, 13 November 2026, at the J. F. Ade Ajayi Main Auditorium, University of Lagos. What will it take to make credit more accessible to African businesses and individuals? At the fourth edition of Africa Credit Expo (ACE) 202 6, stakeholders across financial services, technology, policy, investment and entrepreneurship examined the role of reliable credit information, financial inclusion and collaboration in expanding access to capital. Powered by CreditRegistry and supported by Afreximbank , the Expo was held on Friday, 13 November 2026, at the J. F. Ade Ajayi Main Auditorium, University of Lagos. Themed “Reimagining Africa’s Credit Economy: Unlocking Capital, Trust and Opportunity,” the event provided a platform for conversations on the systems, innovations and partnerships shaping the future of credit across the continent. Building Trust and Expanding Access to Capital Discussions at the Expo explored the role of credible credit information in building trust between lenders and borrowers. Reliable data enables financial institutions to assess risk more effectively and make informed lending decisions, while individuals and businesses with established credit histories are better positioned to demonstrate their credit worthiness. The conversations also considered the financing constraints facing micro, small and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs). Despite their contribution to employment and economic activity, many small businesses continue to encounter barriers to affordable financing. Improving access to relevant financial products and strengthening credit information systems remain important to addressing these gaps. Technology, Financial Inclusion and the Next Generation Digital innovation and data intelligence featured prominently in discussions about the future of credit. Alternative credit assessment approaches have the potential to broaden access for individuals and businesses with limited formal credit histories. However, the expansion of digital financial services must be accompanied by responsible lending practices, consumer protection and transparency. The Expo also placed attention on young people through student-focused sessions and discussions on financial literacy. These conversations connected access to credit with the need for individuals to understand financial management, borrowing and long-term wealth creation. This focus reflects the February 2026 memorandum of understanding between CreditRegistry and the University of Lagos, through its Entrepreneurship and Skills Development Centre (ESDC), to integrate the Africa Consumer Credit Academy (ACCA) curriculum into the Centre’s programmes. The initiative is intended to strengthen financial literacy through learning opportunities, mentorship, certification and engagement with industry. top.title: Arash Markazi on CNN: The NFL wants to own every holiday
top.description: The Sporting Tribune founder and CEO Arash Markazi joined CNN on Thursday, fresh off covering the Rams' 26-13 win over the Green Bay Packers at SoFi Stadium, to talk about the NFL's growing grip on the holiday calendar. The league has played on Thanksgiving for decades and now has games scheduled on Thanksgiving Eve, Black Friday, Christmas and New Year's Eve, with the Super Bowl falling on Valentine's Day this season. Markazi said the strategy is simple. "Football is king in this country," Markazi said, noting that NFL games make up the vast majority of the most-watched broadcasts in the country each year. He said the league targets days when families are together and nobody is working, so it can reach casual viewers as well as die-hard fans. "Where can we get the periphery fans?" Markazi said. "Where can we get the people who don't normally watch?" Markazi was at SoFi Stadium on Wednesday night for the NFL's Thanksgiving Eve game on Netflix, which included a U2 performance, and said the event delivered. "It felt like a mini Super Bowl," he said. "If there were any concerns about how Thanksgiving Eve would do, that was laid to rest. It will be here for a long time." Markazi traced the shift back to Christmas Day, which used to belong to the NBA. "Christmas Day was basketball," he said. "They said, 'No, no, no. Christmas Day is our day too.'" He also broke down Amazon's Black Friday game, which is being made available beyond Prime members this year as the company leans into shopping during the broadcast. "Most people are home on Black Friday, they're shopping," Markazi said. "And now a sports fan can be watching the football game and shopping at the same time." The conversation ended with Aaron Rodgers, whose public split with the Pittsburgh Steelers after being benched and released has become one of the stories of the season. "This is better than anything on Bravo," Markazi said. "This is better than 'Real Housewives.'" Markazi called Rodgers a first-ballot Hall of Famer and "maybe a top-five quarterback of all time," but said the drama likely marks the end of his career. "No one needs this kind of baggage," he said. "But you want to talk about going out in a blaze of glory."

top.title: Germany's Freigang banned over drugs test issues
top.description: Laura Freigang has scored 17 goals in 45 appearances for Germany [Getty Images] Germany international Laura Freigang has been suspended from football for 16 months over issues with three drugs tests. The 28-year-old will miss the Women's World Cup next summer and is banned from all football activity until after 7 October 2027. The 16-month suspension begins from the date of notification by the German Football Association (DFB), which took place in June. The World Anti-Doping Agency (Wada), the National Anti-Doping Agency (Nada), DFB and Freigang reached a dispute resolution agreement. The dispute said Entracht Frankfurt forward Freigang committed three reporting and/or testing failures between 11 March 2025 and 23 February 2026. Freigang can return to training two months prior to the end of the suspension period but cannot play matches until after 7 October. All personal records of appearances, goals, assists or other statistics from 23 February 2026 are nullified, though Frankfurt's results are unaffected. This season Freigang has scored six goals and provided two assists in 11 starts in the Frauen-Bundesliga. Since joining the club in 2020, the striker has scored 107 goals in 187 appearances and was in the Germany squad for October's friendly victories over Australia and Japan. In a club statement , Franfurt said they will "begin discussions shortly to determine the terms of her future employment relationship". Freigang's current contract is due to expire on 30 June 2027. Frankfurt's director of women's football Katharina Kiel said: "The agreement now reached provides clarity and planning security in a process unprecedented for Eintracht Frankfurt - for us as a club, but above all for Laura. "The way she and the team have handled the situation in recent months, and how Laura personally led by example with her performance on the pitch during a very difficult time, deserves the highest recognition. "The identified shortcomings, despite the agreement to settle the dispute, have resulted in a suspension, which means the loss of a key player." top.title: Skip Bayless’ scathing Mike McCarthy nickname resurfaces after Aaron Rodgers sleeping claims
top.description: Photo by Lauren Leigh Bacho/Getty Images Skip Bayless’ old criticism of Mike McCarthy has resurfaced after Aaron Rodgers accused the Pittsburgh Steelers head coach of falling asleep during team meetings. The NFL pundit gave McCarthy the nickname ‘Mike McSleepy’ back in 2021, and his comments have taken on a new relevance following Rodgers’ recent allegations. Rodgers claimed McCarthy arrived late to a quarterbacks’ meeting, fell asleep twice while snoring loudly and then walked out without explanation. The former Green Bay Packers quarterback suggested this was not an isolated incident, as similar behaviour had taken place during their previous years together. However, this is not the first time McCarthy has faced questions about his alertness during games and meetings. Bayless famously took aim at the coach on Fox Sports’ Undisputed after the Dallas Cowboys suffered a 23-19 defeat to the New York Giants in January 2021. The Cowboys entered that game at 6-9 and needed a victory to keep their playoff hopes alive. Instead, they lost to the Giants and missed the postseason, prompting Bayless to deliver a lengthy rant about McCarthy’s role on the sideline. “What have I had a problem with all year long? I’ve sat over here and said this 100 times this season. I keep asking: What does Mike McCarthy do on the sideline? He doesn’t call plays; he doesn’t overrule or rule on special teams; he just sort of stands over there with his hands in his pockets, blinking and looking around like, ‘Am I the head coach?’ I’m not sure. “Mike McCarthy is Mike McSleepy. He has challenged two plays the whole year and I’m saying, ‘Who is he and what is he doing over there?’ You know what a pond looks like with a frog on a lilypad; he’s like a big old bullfrog on a lilypad just sunning himself on Sunday afternoon.” Bayless’ comments have resurfaced amid the growing controversy surrounding McCarthy’s treatment of Rodgers and the 42-year-old’s departure from Pittsburgh. top.title: Tech's outage problem needs maintenance, not conspiracy theories
top.description: Years of technical debt, increasingly complex systems, and underinvestment in IT operations have left organizations vulnerable to major outages, according to Forrester. The analyst pointed to a seven-day stretch in November when failures disrupted Microsoft 365, US air traffic control, banking, and other critical services. The coinciding outages provoked "a slew of conspiracy theories about cyberattacks and AI," Forrester said. "The real culprit is tragically mundane: the culmination of decades of technical debt, the frenetic buildout of massively complex and highly interdependent systems, the concentration of risk, and the underinvestment in advanced operations." Forrester urged technology suppliers and in-house IT teams to prioritize resilience as their systems grow more complex. Otherwise, "the tech estate will collapse like a house of cards, taking down consumer and business trust with it." Earlier this month, Microsoft was left struggling to restore many of its cloud services after a core process running on some servers became "overwhelmed" and its attempts to fix the problem failed. Some of its services did not recover for another 24 hours. In October, Google Cloud blamed a "power event" for taking down multiple online products for customers in Western Europe. Affected services included BigQuery Data Transfer Service, Cloud Filestore, Cloud Run, Google App Engine, and Google Kubernetes Engine. In October last year , a major outage impacted Amazon Web Services (AWS), with even Amazon's own web page reported to be offline and dozens of other online services and websites affected. Aviation and banking were also hit this month. A communications outage triggered a nationwide ground stop in the US on November 13 , while incidents involving JPMorgan Chase, United Airlines, Apple, Workday, Gmail, and other services added to the sense of widespread instability. "Claims that these were all part of one connected cyberattack or conspiracy are highly unlikely. The real story is much more mundane," the report said . Forrester argued that organizations have prioritized visible improvements over repairs to the underlying technology. "Modernization investments have favored visible change over structural renewal," wrote report authors Lauren Nelson and Mark Moccia. "Organizations routinely fund new customer experiences, cloud migrations, platform consolidation, and AI initiatives because leaders can connect them to growth or productivity. "They are less enthusiastic about updating core systems, simplifying architectures, retiring obsolete components, and eliminating fragile interfaces. The result is a modern front end resting on an aging, brittle, and increasingly interconnected estate." Forrester's recommendations are to map dependencies, test failures and recovery under realistic conditions, and use incidents and near misses to identify weaknesses before they cause another outage. ®

top.title: JJ Redick Reveals When He Was Convinced Lakers Had To Sign Ziaire Williams
top.description: Mandatory Credit: Jon Endow-Imagn Images The Los Angeles Lakers brought in many new faces this past offseason, and Ziaire Williams has proven to be one of their better acquisitions. There wasn’t much hype about Williams’ arrival, but Lakers head coach JJ Redick revealed at Wednesday’s practice that all it took was one meeting to convince him they had to sign the forward. “I’ve been collecting intel on players for 20 years now,” Redick said, via Infanity TV. “I did it as a player, I did it in media, I do it now as a coach, so yeah you certainly want to bring the right people in here… Ziaire was supposed to make six and a half million, I think, from Brooklyn this year, and then he was a non-guaranteed deal, so they waive him. “He becomes a free agent, and he was willing to go to a gym in Vegas and work out for our coaching staff and for Rob [Pelinka],” Redick continued. “We put him through that; he looked great. I met with him the next day at the hotel for about 45 minutes, and towards the middle of that conversation, I just kept thinking to myself, holy s***, we got to get this guy in our locker room. We need this guy to be a Laker.” Williams hit free agency after the Brooklyn Nets didn’t pick up his $6.25 million team option for 2026-27. The Lakers were immediately linked to the 25-year-old , as he had fans inside their facility. Redick then joined that group of fans after meeting Williams for the first time. The 42-year-old felt the Lakers had to get him in, and it doesn’t look like they faced much competition. Why? Well, the Lakers signed Williams to just a one-year, $3 million deal . That’s looking like quite a bargain now. Williams is averaging 9.1 points, 2.3 rebounds, 1.7 assists, 1.2 steals, and 0.1 blocks per game in 2026-27 while shooting 53.8% from the field and 42.1% from beyond the arc. He has been the kind of athletic 3-and-D wing the Lakers have been crying out for in recent years. Williams also said in the offseason that Lakers fans can expect a lot of energy and hard work from him on the court . He has been true to his word and is becoming a fan favorite. With role players like Williams impressing and superstar guard Luka Doncic on a tear, the Lakers have gotten off to an excellent 15-3 start to the season. Not many expected them to have the best record in the NBA, but it has now been claimed that this is down to an easy schedule. Well, the Lakers will get a chance to make a statement as they take on the 15-4 San Antonio Spurs next at Frost Bank Center on Friday at 9:30 p.m. ET.

top.title: Max Verstappen and George Russell rivalry "really cool for the sport", says F1 pundit
top.description: Motorsport photo The Las Vegas Grand Prix weekend reignited the long-running tension between Red Bull and Mercedes drivers, Max Verstappen and George Russell , and it was the talking point of Sky's F1 Show podcast this week. Three-time W Series champion and Sky Sports pundit Jamie Chadwick discussed the reignited rivalry on the podcast, claiming that no other driver gets under Verstappen's skin as much as Russell. Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing, George Russell, Mercedes Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing, George Russell, Mercedes "On one side it's really cool for the sport to have this kind of rivalry because it gets everyone talking. top.title: Why Lions might franchise tag Brian Branch instead of signing a contract extension
top.description: Why Lions might franchise tag Brian Branch instead of signing a contract extension originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Detroit Lions are facing off against the Chicago Bears on Thanksgiving, and defensive back Brian Branch is going to be key to stopping this high-powered Bears offense. For Branch himself, this week is a huge opportunity to further prove himself in a contract year. Set to hit the open market after 2026, alongside tight end Sam LaPorta, the Lions will have a difficult decision to make with Branch this upcoming offseason. ESPN's Bill Barnwell believes that, instead of a contract extension for Branch, he might be in line for the Lions' franchise tag. The reason why is simple: it's more affordable for Detroit to use the tag on Branch to give them more time to figure out a long-term deal. Why Brian Branch might be franchise tagged by Lions "With the safety franchise tag projected to come in at $22.2 million, the Lions might see tagging him as a logical way to continue their relationship while they negotiate a long-term extension," Barnwell writes. With the Lions having plenty of offseason questions to solve, once the 2026 season comes to a close, being able to tag Branch and figure things out over an extended period of time would be much easier than trying to work out an extension. Since Branch has had an up-and-down NFL career so far, seeing what Branch can do to close out the 2026 NFL season could give the Lions reason to sign him to a long-term deal. But even if he doesn't finish strong, the Lions could still elect to tag him to avoid letting him hit free agency, where he'd surely get plenty of competitive offers from other teams looking for upgrades. Branch has a lot on the line this year, although he's most likely going to get tagged by the Lions. LaPorta's future is up in the air as well, and he could get tagged, which could complicate Branch's future with the team. While the Lions could still choose LaPorta over Branch, with the team's more questionable secondary, tagging Branch would make a lot of sense as a way to guarantee they have at least one more season out of the star defensive back. nigeria.title: Why Yoro’s red card against Liverpool was overturned – FA panel
nigeria.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye The Football Association has released the written reasons for overturning Leny Yoro’s red card for Manchester United against Liverpool, despite refereeing body Pro Ref maintaining that the on-field decision was not clearly wrong. According to Sky Sports, the FA’s independent regulatory commission unanimously ruled that referee Sam Barrott made an “obvious error” in deciding Liverpool striker Alexander Isak had an obvious goalscoring opportunity when Yoro fouled him during United’s 4-0 defeat at Anfield on Sunday. The panel said Isak’s touch was so heavy that he had lost control of the ball, allowing United goalkeeper Senne Lammens to close in and potentially gather it before the striker could shoot. “Taking the foul committed by Yoro out of the scenario, Isak would not have had an obvious goalscoring opportunity,” the commission said in its written reasons. The decision overturned Yoro’s one-match suspension, making the defender available for United’s Premier League match against Brentford on Saturday. Pro Ref chief refereeing officer Howard Webb had defended the officials’ decision, saying Isak was moving quickly towards the ball and that it was “certainly not clearly wrong” to judge he would reach it before Lammens. United submitted video evidence from several angles, as well as footage of Brighton defender Pascal Struijk’s red card against Sunderland, which was overturned after an appeal. The club also argued that Isak would have been at least 1.8 metres short of the ball without Yoro’s challenge. The commission said it could not test the validity of United’s distance analysis and therefore viewed it with caution. A separate Premier League Key Match Incidents panel is reported to have backed the original decision; its findings for the matchweek are due to be published on December 2. nigeria.title: 2027 election: Atiku, Amaechi have best experience in governance — Dele Momodu
nigeria.description: The Deputy Director-General, Media and Communication of the African Democratic Congress, Dele Momodu, has described former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar and former Rivers State Governor Rotimi Amaechi as politicians with the best experience in governance ahead of the 2027 presidential election. Momodu said the duo had the experience and capacity to tackle Nigeria’s challenges, expressing confidence that Atiku could revive moribund industries, including the Ajaokuta Steel Company, by engaging competent professionals. He spoke in an interview on Trust TV on Thursday, while defending Atiku’s ability to deliver on his promises if elected president in 2027. Momodu said he believed in Atiku’s leadership ability, citing his success in business and willingness to deploy expertise in addressing difficult national challenges. “Nothing is impossible with the determination of a leader, and I know Alhaji Atiku Abubakar to be a very different kind of leader, and that’s why he’s been able to run his own business successfully,” he said. The ADC chieftain said Atiku’s promise to revamp the Ajaokuta Steel Company should not be interpreted as a plan to repeat past approaches, but as an opportunity to bring in professionals with the requisite expertise to restore the facility. “If he tells you that he will revamp Ajaokuta, it does not mean that he will do it the way they did it decades ago. He will bring in the best expert,” Momodu said. He cited the revival of Nigeria’s railway system under the administration of former President Muhammadu Buhari as an example of how leadership and competent personnel could transform infrastructure previously considered beyond recovery. Momodu credited Amaechi, who served as Minister of Transportation under Buhari, with delivering railway projects that restored public confidence in train transportation across parts of the country. “You can see even while President Buhari was in power, there was a man who was able to do and deliver so many projects, and that man is the Right Honourable Chibuke Rotimi Amaechi,” he said. According to Momodu, Nigerians had previously lost hope in the railway system but became proud of the trains following the projects executed during Amaechi’s tenure. “People gave up on our trains, that the railways will never function again in Nigeria. But you can see within a short time, we were all very proud to show off our trains as they moved in different parts of Nigeria,” he said. He expressed optimism that a combination of Atiku’s experience and Amaechi’s record in infrastructure development would deliver better governance if they worked together in 2027. “So the same thing will happen if you bring in Atiku Amaechi together in 2027. These guys have the best experience in governance,” Momodu added. The post 2027 election: Atiku, Amaechi have best experience in governance — Dele Momodu appeared first on Vanguard News .

nigeria.title: Nathaniel Bassey builds subsidised apartments for staff, musicians
nigeria.description: Gospel singer Nathaniel Bassey has revealed that he has built apartments for his staff and musicians under a housing scheme designed to help them become homeowners. The singer disclosed this in an Instagram post, where he shared his excitement about seeing the beneficiaries move into their homes with their families by Christmas. Bassey said the project, which he named Love Song Apartments, was driven by his long-standing desire to help members of his team own houses. He explained that the housing scheme required the beneficiaries to contribute a significant portion of the cost, while the apartments were offered to them at highly subsidised rates. According to him, he provided a family-owned plot of land and contributed funds towards the project, while his friend, Peter Chubby of Danville Mall, partnered with him through a joint venture arrangement. The singer said construction began gradually, with the team building the apartments in phases. “One thing I realised doing this was that we used to be told musicians were not organised. But with the right guidance, they can do great things. They have committed to this. See, you never know what you can do until you try,” he wrote. Bassey said he was particularly delighted at the prospect of seeing the beneficiaries settle into their fully owned apartments with their children enjoying the play area provided within the estate. He described the project as an expression of his belief that leadership should involve extending opportunities and blessings to others. “This is never to brag. I’m not that kind of person. But sometimes, people need to see these things to know God is faithful,” he added. The singer also disclosed that the housing project was only its first phase, expressing hope that more apartments would be developed in the future. He said he hoped to share the knowledge and experience gained from the initiative with other creatives and musicians in the Christian community to encourage them to pursue similar projects. Bassey further emphasised the importance of leaders carrying their team members along as they achieve personal success, saying that a leader should not be the only one enjoying the benefits of progress. “Finally, as a leader, if you are the only one sharing testimonies, after a while, those around you will soon be despondent. nigeria.title: Mock Accreditation: INEC Faces Crucial Test As 100 Million Voters Await 2027 Elections
nigeria.description: With exactly 50 days before Nigerians return to the ballot, the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) is preparing for a nationwide test that could offer an important indication of whether the country is ready for another fiercely contested general election. On Saturday, November 28, the electoral umpire will deploy its Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) and electronic results upload technology across 17,676 selected polling units in a mock exercise designed to identify operational weaknesses, test equipment reliability and strengthen public confidence ahead of the 2027 elections. The exercise, scheduled for 8:30 a.m. to 2:30 p.m., will cover two polling units in each of the country’s 8,838 registration areas, giving INEC an opportunity to assess the performance of its electoral technology across different locations before the presidential and National Assembly elections on January 16, 2027, and the governorship and State Houses of Assembly elections on February 6. #OsunDecides2026: Election Officers Take Delivery Of Materials, Mobilise To Polling Units during the Osun State governorship election on August 15, 2026. It comes against the backdrop of lingering controversies surrounding the 2023 general elections, particularly the failure to upload presidential election results to the INEC Result Viewing Portal (IReV) in real time, technical difficulties associated with BVAS and allegations of electoral irregularities. Chairman of INEC, Joash Amupitan, described the mock exercise as an important part of preparations for the forthcoming elections, while urging Nigerians to participate. According to her, the commission has reduced the accreditation threshold to 850 voters per BVAS device, with additional machines to be provided at polling units with larger voter populations. The exercise will also test the electronic upload of results to IReV, although Meci acknowledged that successful transmission would depend on network availability. 100 Million Voters, 176,846 Polling Units The scale of the preparations reflects the size of Nigeria’s electorate. INEC says it is now managing a verified national register of more than 100 million voters after removing over 1.6 million invalid, duplicated, and deceased records from the previous register of approximately 103 million. Amupitan disclosed on Wednesday, during a meeting with resident electoral commissioners from the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory, that the clean-up followed the application of an Automated Biometric Identification System and a statutory claims-and-objections audit. He said direct flights would facilitate trade and tourism, promote educational exchanges and strengthen ties between Nigerians and Tunisians. The minister also called for greater private-sector participation in bilateral economic relations, urging Nigerian companies, including the Dangote Group, to explore investment opportunities in Tunisia. Speaking during the meeting, Moshen disclosed that bilateral trade between Nigeria and Tunisia had increased from $7 million to more than $100 million by 2024. The Tunisian ambassador also reaffirmed his country’s commitment to maintaining its annual scholarship allocation for Nigerian students. In response, Enikanolaiye said he would work with relevant government institutions to facilitate access to the scholarship opportunities for eligible Nigerians. He also called for increased cooperation between both countries in French-language education. The minister further expressed Nigeria’s readiness to work towards convening the sixth session of the Nigeria–Tunisia Joint Commission in the first quarter of 2027. nigeria.title: Senate probes LPG exports over domestic supply shortage
nigeria.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — The Senate has raised concerns over inadequate supply of Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG) to the domestic market, warning that the shortfall could undermine efforts to reduce the price of cooking gas in the country. The Senate Committee on Gas Resources, chaired by Senator Jarigbe Jarigbe (APC, Cross River North), raised the concern on Thursday during an interface with stakeholders in the gas sector on export revenue remittances and domestic LPG supply. The meeting, held at the National Assembly complex, Abuja, was convened to examine the availability of LPG in the domestic market, export volumes and revenue remittances from the country’s gas sector. Jarigbe said the situation was contrary to the objectives of Presidential Executive Order 9, signed by President Bola Tinubu on February 13, 2026, which seeks to improve oil and gas revenue remittances to the Federation Account. He said the government also needed to ensure adequate domestic gas supply to reduce the financial burden on Nigerians. “LPG has to be supplied to the domestic market for the good of the common man as intended with Executive Order 9 issued by President Tinubu to ameliorate the sufferings of the masses on price of gas,” he said. The executive order, however, focuses primarily on oil and gas revenue remittances rather than expressly mandating domestic LPG supply. Speaking to journalists after the meeting, the lawmaker said the committee was determined to establish the reasons for the inadequate supply and work towards bringing down cooking gas prices. “We are already working for Nigerians here, for our people, and that’s why we want to get to the root of it. “And we’ll make sure that the price of gas goes down, because when there is adequate supply in response to demand, the price will naturally go down,” he said. Jarigbe said industry operators had attributed the export of some LPG to the ratio of propane to butane in the product. He, however, argued that the composition could be adjusted through blending to make more of the product suitable for domestic consumption. “They give an excuse that the ratio of propane to butane is 80-20, and that’s what they export. But it’s a matter of blending, so that it will be the reverse: the quantity of butane will be 80 per cent, while the quantity of propane will be 20 per cent for local consumption in Nigeria,” he said. nigeria.title: ‘I have no time for anybody’ – Okpebholo denies involvement in NDC Edo attack
nigeria.description: Edo State Governor, Monday Okpebholo, has dismissed allegations linking him to the attack on supporters of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) in Benin City, saying he has no time for those accusing him. Okpebholo spoke on Thursday at an All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign rally in Ehor, the administrative headquarters of Uhunmwonde Local Government Area, a day after gunmen attacked NDC supporters who had gathered along Airport Road to welcome the party’s presidential candidate, Peter Obi, to the state. The governor described the allegations against him as lies, insisting that he did not use thugs during his previous political campaigns. “Yesterday some people were crying because when they thought they would come to Edo and shine, when they got here, they met only three people in the hall. They started shooting themselves because they want to spoil our name. They started calling my name but I have no time for anybody. They are lying,” he said. He added that hearing his name mentioned during a television report made him conclude that the claims being circulated about him were untrue. Okpebholo also denied using thugs during his political campaigns, recalling his contests for the Senate and governorship. “When I was contesting for Senate, I didn’t use thugs. When I was contesting for governor, I did not use thugs,” he said. The governor further claimed that the NDC chairman was among those previously implicated in the killing of his police officer, but said he had refrained from pursuing the matter to avoid accusations of political victimisation. “The NDC chairman was one of those that were fingered at that time. If I start now, they will say that I am victimising them because of politics,” he added. The attack occurred on Wednesday along Airport Road in Benin City, where gunmen reportedly opened fire on people waiting to receive Obi ahead of his town hall meeting in the state. The Edo State Police Command said three gunmen in a black Toyota Hilux opened fire after encountering police operatives stationed at the airport exit gate. One person, identified as Aimionkhale Micheal, sustained gunshot injuries to his thighs and was taken to hospital. The police said Commissioner of Police Patrick Daaor had ordered an investigation and directed tactical operatives to track down the fleeing suspects. The NDC condemned the incident and called for an investigation into the attack. As of Thursday, the police had not publicly identified the suspects or announced any arrests. Bwala said this during an interview on the Niger Unfiltered podcast, published on Thursday, following questions about why Tinubu had granted only one official interview to Nigerian media organisations in about three years and seven months in office. “I expect us to do more. And the second time, you’ll see more of that,” Bwala said. He acknowledged that some interviews had been postponed at short notice, saying the President had sometimes agreed to meet journalists before later rescheduling. “There are a number of times in which the President called for media. At the 11th hour, he may have been advised, and then he would apologise and say some other time,” Bwala said. The presidential aide said Tinubu was willing to speak with journalists and did not need prepared answers or prior briefings before interviews. “There is a willingness to grant interviews on the part of the President. Bwala defended the Presidency’s right to choose the journalists and platforms it engages, saying it should not be pressured to grant interviews to specific media organisations. “We control our narrative. He said State House press corps members representing mainstream, new, social and print media covered the President’s daily activities. “In the State House press corps, we have representatives of the mainstream, the new media, the social media, and the print media. nigeria.title: FCCPC urges supermarkets to protect consumer trust
nigeria.description: The Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Commission (FCCPC) has urged supermarket and shopping mall operators across the country to strengthen consumer protection practices and earn customers’ trust through transparent business operations. The Executive Vice Chairman of the commission, Mr Tunji Bello, gave the advice through the Lagos Zonal Coordinator, Dr Olubunmi Otti, at a one-day sectoral roundtable on compliance and enforcement of the Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Act (FCCPA) 2018, held in Lagos. The engagement, themed, “Compliance Obligations of Supermarket Operators,” was organised to sensitise operators on their responsibilities under the law, particularly as the yuletide shopping season approaches. Bello said supermarkets had become essential to millions of Nigerians, serving as major outlets for purchasing food, medicines, children’s necessities and other household essentials. He said customers placed their health, money and trust in the hands of supermarket operators whenever they patronised their businesses, adding that such trust must be protected. “The supermarket is no longer just a shop for millions of Nigerians; it is where they buy their food, medicine, children’s needs and daily essentials. “When a consumer walks into your store, they are placing their trust, their health and hard-earned money in your hands. That trust must be protected,” he said. The FCCPC boss said the FCCPA 2018 empowered the commission to protect consumers, promote fair competition and ensure that businesses operated transparently and accountably. He said the roundtable focused on the commission’s role in guiding compliance, consumer rights under the Act, safety standards in retail outlets, the legal framework and complaint resolution mechanisms. Bello disclosed that the commission received complaints daily concerning the supermarket sector, including discrepancies between shelf prices and prices charged at checkout points, the sale of expired or nearly expired products without clear disclosure, misleading promotions and discounts, poor refund and return policies, and inadequate product information. He cited the experience of a mother who budgeted N50,000 for monthly shopping but encountered higher prices at the payment counter, describing such discrepancies as a breach of consumer trust rather than a mere mistake. He said the commission’s objective was to reduce and ultimately eliminate such complaints, not to shut down businesses, but to help operators understand and comply with their obligations. “Compliance is not a burden; compliance is good business,” he said, adding that customers who trusted a supermarket’s products and refund policies were more likely to return. The engagement attracted representatives of supermarket and retail businesses, including Justrite Superstores, Jendol Superstores, Prince Ebeano Supermarkets, Sundry Foods and Edichat Pharmacy and Stores. He also announced the award of the sum of N100 million to the families of each military personnel who died in the crash, separate from the houses. The President made the announcement on Thursday during a memorial service and wreath-laying ceremony held in honour of the victims of the NAF ATR 42 aircraft accident. He said the houses, located in the Renewed Hope Housing Project in Abuja, would be allocated to the immediate families of the deceased military personnel and civilians who were aboard the aircraft. The president pointed out that the gesture would also be extended to the immediate families of the civilians on board the aircraft. “In addition to the flats, these officers would receive from this government N100m each,” he said. He assured the bereaved families that the government would remain committed to supporting them beyond the memorial ceremony. “Long after the wreaths have faded, our commitment to these families must remain evergreen,” Tinubu said. The president also assured Nigerians that the October 5 aircraft crash would be thoroughly investigated, promising that the findings would inform improvements in military and civilian aviation safety. “I assure the grieving nation that this accident will be thoroughly investigated. We will seek answers. We will learn the lessons. We will strengthen our military and civilian aviation safety standards. Our operational procedures and our institutional accountability will be strengthened. “We owe them the truth, and we will honour that debt,” he said. Tinubu further reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to improving the welfare, safety and operational capacity of the Armed Forces through modernisation, training and better equipment. “A nation that asks its sons and daughters to fly into danger must give them the best wings it can build,” he added. Sources at the centre confided in Vanguard that seven condemned prison inmates actually planned their escape, out of which two – Segun and Abraham – now declared wanted, were lucky. They had been planning their escape for about seven months. The rooms of the condemned prison inmates are said to be secluded and often dark, as they’re not supposed to go out like others. Vanguard also gathered that once in a while, when the condemned inmates go out to do social services, they are always heavily guarded. It was further gathered that for the seven months, they used a chisel to gradually opened the wall of their room, to create enough hole space for them to escape into the premises. Vanguard also gathered that they used posters to cover the space (inside and outside) so that no staff could easily notice their escape plan. It was further gathered that the Correctional Centre fence, about 17 feet high, was topped with embedded broken glass rather than a wire mesh. Furthermore, there is no CCTV camera covering inmates’ movements. D-Day On the day of escape, they got thick blankets which they tied together to make a long thick rope, and hooked it to the broken glasses on top of the fence. It was with this blanket-rope that the condemned inmates climbed over the tall fence and escaped to the other side, said a source. But after Segun and Abraham had scaled the fence, the blanket became weak. So it gave way, and the other five would-be escapees fell back on the prison premises. Vanguard also gathered that fully armed officers of the center, who were supposed to be on 24/7 surveillance to secure the other side of the fence, weren’t there to arrest the condemned inmates. nigeria.title: ‘I bought book on how to have boy-child’ – Makinde
nigeria.description: By Angel Aniobi Oyo State Governor, Seyi Makinde has revealed that he bought a book and ovulation kits with his wife in their attempt to have a male child after welcoming two daughters. Makinde made this disclosure during an interview with media personality Chude Jideonwo, where he spoke about his family, fatherhood and the decision to have a third child. Recounting how they planned their family, the governor said he initially wanted just one child but reluctantly agreed to have two after his wife questioned why they should have only one. According to him, he was comfortable with having two daughters and did not consider the gender of his children important. “Gender doesn’t mean anything to me because I felt whether a girl or a boy, it’s all linked up to how you’re going to bring them up and how you set them up to impact their environment, and you can do it with any kid,” he said. Makinde, however, explained that cultural expectations and comments from his mother-in-law amplified his wife’s desire to have a male child. He said his mother-in-law told his wife that Yoruba men whose wives did not give birth to boys could seek to have a male child outside their marriages. “I’m a Yoruba man, but I think I am okay with the girls that God has blessed us with,” he recalled saying. The governor disclosed that it took more than five years for him to understand his wife’s desire to have a son, after which they agreed to explore ways of having a male child. He said he subsequently purchased a book on how to conceive a boy, which they both read and followed, alongside purchasing ovulation kits. “So, I said, okay, well, that’s fine. We have to go and buy a book on how to have a boy, and then we’ll read it and apply strictly,” he said. Makinde added that their efforts eventually resulted in the birth of their son, who became their third child. “That was it. The prosecution said the man had “admitted” to speeding when his car collided with the tanker, “causing the steering wheel to slip from his hands and his car to veer off course”. When the car hit the truck, one of its tyres exploded, causing it to overturn, the prosecution said. The fire erupted as a result of a petrol leak, it added. More than 20 million people live in Greater Cairo, a sprawling and dense metropolis. business.title: Bitcoin Has Become Boring, Finally
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Has Become Boring, Finally The 2019 Lightning conference in Berlin was lit: five hundred “cypherpunks” getting each other high on visions of a future with peer-to-peer electronic cash. Attending a bitcoin conference back in the day felt like being a teenager at a friend’s party while their parents were out of town. It was exciting and new. The feeling was the opposite of FOMO: something big was happening, we were on the inside, and the rest of the world was going to envy us. It was the kind of party that you could only have when the adults weren’t looking. Whenever someone bought a beer (with bitcoin), everyone would hoot and holler and record it on their phones for Instagram/Twitter (it was still called Twitter). Lightning was the bleeding edge. We called it “the Lightning Network” (capitalized, if you please), and talking about it felt like talking about string theory: something so far out you’re not even sure it’s real. I spent a lot of time invoking the abacus . Those are the times some of us remember fondly and keep trying to relive at bitcoin conferences today. That’s why we engage in rituals like drone shows, Satoshi Rockamoto sets, beefsteak dinners , and video game tournaments for sats, but it’s not the same. The ratio of bitcoin OG speakers to suits is shifting. Many event rooms are half empty, and the halls and meeting rooms are full of people negotiating cap tables and profit-sharing splits. The adults haven’t shut the party down, but they have crashed it, and it kinda feels like their party now. The most exciting thing I noticed at the last bitcoin conference I attended was that nothing exciting happened. And that’s worth celebrating. From Tech Subcultures to Mainstream Tech Adoption The road to boring is seldom smooth. Technological innovation benefits from passion and bold ideas. People work harder on a project when they feel strongly about it and identify closely with like-minded collaborators. That’s where tech subcultures, their rituals, and their dogmas come from. But such passion and tribalism feed conflict, at least for a while until the tech goes mainstream, and normies, who couldn’t care less about subculture squabbles, take over. This progression from an exciting new technology that inspires strong emotions to a humdrum utility is not unusual. World-changing innovations often (always?) start with a committed subculture that identifies fiercely with their weird tech before the mainstream adopts it and soon expects it. In fact, this trajectory has become the standard doctrine of tech marketing. Ade Ajayi Main Auditorium, University of Lagos. What will it take to make credit more accessible to African businesses and individuals? At the fourth edition of Africa Credit Expo (ACE) 202 6, stakeholders across financial services, technology, policy, investment and entrepreneurship examined the role of reliable credit information, financial inclusion and collaboration in expanding access to capital. Powered by CreditRegistry and supported by Afreximbank , the Expo was held on Friday, 13 November 2026, at the J. F. Ade Ajayi Main Auditorium, University of Lagos. Themed “Reimagining Africa’s Credit Economy: Unlocking Capital, Trust and Opportunity,” the event provided a platform for conversations on the systems, innovations and partnerships shaping the future of credit across the continent. Building Trust and Expanding Access to Capital Discussions at the Expo explored the role of credible credit information in building trust between lenders and borrowers. Reliable data enables financial institutions to assess risk more effectively and make informed lending decisions, while individuals and businesses with established credit histories are better positioned to demonstrate their credit worthiness. The conversations also considered the financing constraints facing micro, small and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs). Despite their contribution to employment and economic activity, many small businesses continue to encounter barriers to affordable financing. Improving access to relevant financial products and strengthening credit information systems remain important to addressing these gaps. Technology, Financial Inclusion and the Next Generation Digital innovation and data intelligence featured prominently in discussions about the future of credit. Alternative credit assessment approaches have the potential to broaden access for individuals and businesses with limited formal credit histories. However, the expansion of digital financial services must be accompanied by responsible lending practices, consumer protection and transparency. The Expo also placed attention on young people through student-focused sessions and discussions on financial literacy. These conversations connected access to credit with the need for individuals to understand financial management, borrowing and long-term wealth creation. This focus reflects the February 2026 memorandum of understanding between CreditRegistry and the University of Lagos, through its Entrepreneurship and Skills Development Centre (ESDC), to integrate the Africa Consumer Credit Academy (ACCA) curriculum into the Centre’s programmes. The initiative is intended to strengthen financial literacy through learning opportunities, mentorship, certification and engagement with industry. Speaking on Monday, 23 November 2026, on the theme “The Dual-Mandate NCE-Degree Programme: Prospects, Challenges and the Future of Teacher Education in Nigeria,” he described the programme as an important opportunity to reposition teacher education. For decades, Colleges of Education depended on university affiliations to award Bachelor’s degrees, despite many possessing the academic capacity to run such programmes. The Federal Colleges of Education Act 2023 changed this, empowering eligible institutions to award degrees independently. Under the Dual-Mandate programme, students can complete three years of NCE training and proceed to another two years for a Bachelor’s degree in Education. Dr. Olowolafe explained that combining practical teaching skills with deeper academic knowledge would produce better-prepared educators. However, he cautioned that institutional autonomy must be supported by sustained funding, improved curricula and professional development. With Nigeria facing an estimated shortage of one million teachers, he also called for greater integration of vocational education, artificial intelligence and digital skills into learning. “AI can explain a quadratic equation at midnight, but it cannot offer the steady, empathetic guidance of a caring adult,” he said, emphasizing that artificial intelligence must complement, not replace, the human qualities of effective teaching. During the lecture, Dr. Olowolafe announced that the Tunji Olowolafe Foundation would establish a fully equipped, solar-powered Gbemisola Olowolafe Memorial ICT Centre (GOMTECH) with high-speed internet connectivity at SACOETEC. entertainment.title: Remembering Pete Edochie: 5 Films That Made Him a Nollywood Legend
entertainment.description: Nollywood icon Pete Edochie, MON, who passed away at the age of 79 in Enugu. Did you grow up watching Pete Edochie in Nollywood films? Then you probably remember that voice. Deep, commanding and unmistakable, it often came with his signature red cap, traditional Igbo attire and a generous helping of proverbs. The actor was just as memorable away from the screen, where his sharp wit, outspoken nature and candid opinions made him a fascinating personality in interviews. He was never one to shy away from saying exactly what he thought, and that straightforwardness became another part of what audiences remembered about him. For generations of Nollywood viewers, Pete Edochie was the actor they could recognise before he had even finished his first sentence. He became one of Nigerian cinema’s most familiar faces, often playing kings, chiefs, fathers and respected elders. His breakthrough came in 1987 when he portrayed Okonkwo in the television adaptation of Chinua Achebe ‘s Things Fall Apart , a performance that helped establish him as one of Nollywood’s most respected actors. The veteran actor passed away in Enugu yesterday, on Wednesday, 25 November 2026, at the age of 79, following a prolonged battle with prostate cancer. Born in Zaria and originally from Ifite Nteje in Anambra State, Edochie began his career in broadcasting in 1967, eventually rising to become Deputy Managing Director of the Anambra Broadcasting Service. He went on to feature in hundreds of films, including Igodo , The Egg of Life and Lionheart . Pete Edochie and Genevieve Nnaji behind the scenes on the set of the 2018 film Lionheart, where they played father and daughter Chief Ernest Obiagu and Adaeze Obiagu. Survived by his wife, Josephine, and their six children, including actors Linc and Yul Edochie , he leaves behind a remarkable body of work. As we remember his life and contribution to Nigerian cinema, here are five films that capture some of the performances that made Pete Edochie a household name. Born on 7 March 1947 in Zaria, Kaduna State, and hailing from Akamnato, Ifite Nteje in Anambra State, Pete Edochie began his career in broadcasting long before becoming a household name on television and cinema screens. At age 20, in 1967, he joined the Eastern Nigeria Broadcasting Service (ENBS)—later the Anambra Broadcasting Service (ABS)—rising steadily through the ranks to serve as Director of Programmes and Deputy Managing Director. His defining breakthrough came in 1987 when he portrayed the fierce, tragic hero Okonkwo in the Nigerian Television Authority’s (NTA) acclaimed television adaptation of Chinua Achebe ‘s Things Fall Apart. Over a screen career spanning nearly four decades, Pete Edochie became synonymous with authority,traditional wisdom, and unforgettable Igbo proverbs. Whether playing stern monarchs, principled elders, or complex patriarchs, he delivered every line with unmistakable gravitas. His extensive filmography includes standout appearances in classics and modern hits alike, such as Things Fall Apart (1987), Igodo (1999), Egg of Life (2003), Oracle (2003), Billionaires Club (2003), End of Money (2005), Lionheart (2018)—where he starred as Chief Ernest Obiagu alongside Genevieve Nnaji—Unroyal (2020), and Foreigner’s God (2022). sports.title: Arash Markazi on CNN: The NFL wants to own every holiday
sports.description: The Sporting Tribune founder and CEO Arash Markazi joined CNN on Thursday, fresh off covering the Rams' 26-13 win over the Green Bay Packers at SoFi Stadium, to talk about the NFL's growing grip on the holiday calendar. The league has played on Thanksgiving for decades and now has games scheduled on Thanksgiving Eve, Black Friday, Christmas and New Year's Eve, with the Super Bowl falling on Valentine's Day this season. Markazi said the strategy is simple. "Football is king in this country," Markazi said, noting that NFL games make up the vast majority of the most-watched broadcasts in the country each year. He said the league targets days when families are together and nobody is working, so it can reach casual viewers as well as die-hard fans. "Where can we get the periphery fans?" Markazi said. "Where can we get the people who don't normally watch?" Markazi was at SoFi Stadium on Wednesday night for the NFL's Thanksgiving Eve game on Netflix, which included a U2 performance, and said the event delivered. "It felt like a mini Super Bowl," he said. "If there were any concerns about how Thanksgiving Eve would do, that was laid to rest. It will be here for a long time." Markazi traced the shift back to Christmas Day, which used to belong to the NBA. "Christmas Day was basketball," he said. "They said, 'No, no, no. Christmas Day is our day too.'" He also broke down Amazon's Black Friday game, which is being made available beyond Prime members this year as the company leans into shopping during the broadcast. "Most people are home on Black Friday, they're shopping," Markazi said. "And now a sports fan can be watching the football game and shopping at the same time." The conversation ended with Aaron Rodgers, whose public split with the Pittsburgh Steelers after being benched and released has become one of the stories of the season. "This is better than anything on Bravo," Markazi said. "This is better than 'Real Housewives.'" Markazi called Rodgers a first-ballot Hall of Famer and "maybe a top-five quarterback of all time," but said the drama likely marks the end of his career. "No one needs this kind of baggage," he said. "But you want to talk about going out in a blaze of glory."

sports.title: Germany's Freigang banned over drugs test issues
sports.description: Laura Freigang has scored 17 goals in 45 appearances for Germany [Getty Images] Germany international Laura Freigang has been suspended from football for 16 months over issues with three drugs tests. The 28-year-old will miss the Women's World Cup next summer and is banned from all football activity until after 7 October 2027. The 16-month suspension begins from the date of notification by the German Football Association (DFB), which took place in June. The World Anti-Doping Agency (Wada), the National Anti-Doping Agency (Nada), DFB and Freigang reached a dispute resolution agreement. The dispute said Entracht Frankfurt forward Freigang committed three reporting and/or testing failures between 11 March 2025 and 23 February 2026. Freigang can return to training two months prior to the end of the suspension period but cannot play matches until after 7 October. All personal records of appearances, goals, assists or other statistics from 23 February 2026 are nullified, though Frankfurt's results are unaffected. This season Freigang has scored six goals and provided two assists in 11 starts in the Frauen-Bundesliga. Since joining the club in 2020, the striker has scored 107 goals in 187 appearances and was in the Germany squad for October's friendly victories over Australia and Japan. In a club statement , Franfurt said they will "begin discussions shortly to determine the terms of her future employment relationship". Freigang's current contract is due to expire on 30 June 2027. Frankfurt's director of women's football Katharina Kiel said: "The agreement now reached provides clarity and planning security in a process unprecedented for Eintracht Frankfurt - for us as a club, but above all for Laura. "The way she and the team have handled the situation in recent months, and how Laura personally led by example with her performance on the pitch during a very difficult time, deserves the highest recognition. "The identified shortcomings, despite the agreement to settle the dispute, have resulted in a suspension, which means the loss of a key player." sports.title: JJ Redick Reveals When He Was Convinced Lakers Had To Sign Ziaire Williams
sports.description: Mandatory Credit: Jon Endow-Imagn Images The Los Angeles Lakers brought in many new faces this past offseason, and Ziaire Williams has proven to be one of their better acquisitions. There wasn’t much hype about Williams’ arrival, but Lakers head coach JJ Redick revealed at Wednesday’s practice that all it took was one meeting to convince him they had to sign the forward. “I’ve been collecting intel on players for 20 years now,” Redick said, via Infanity TV. “I did it as a player, I did it in media, I do it now as a coach, so yeah you certainly want to bring the right people in here… Ziaire was supposed to make six and a half million, I think, from Brooklyn this year, and then he was a non-guaranteed deal, so they waive him. “He becomes a free agent, and he was willing to go to a gym in Vegas and work out for our coaching staff and for Rob [Pelinka],” Redick continued. “We put him through that; he looked great. I met with him the next day at the hotel for about 45 minutes, and towards the middle of that conversation, I just kept thinking to myself, holy s***, we got to get this guy in our locker room. We need this guy to be a Laker.” Williams hit free agency after the Brooklyn Nets didn’t pick up his $6.25 million team option for 2026-27. The Lakers were immediately linked to the 25-year-old , as he had fans inside their facility. Redick then joined that group of fans after meeting Williams for the first time. The 42-year-old felt the Lakers had to get him in, and it doesn’t look like they faced much competition. Why? Well, the Lakers signed Williams to just a one-year, $3 million deal . That’s looking like quite a bargain now. Williams is averaging 9.1 points, 2.3 rebounds, 1.7 assists, 1.2 steals, and 0.1 blocks per game in 2026-27 while shooting 53.8% from the field and 42.1% from beyond the arc. He has been the kind of athletic 3-and-D wing the Lakers have been crying out for in recent years. Williams also said in the offseason that Lakers fans can expect a lot of energy and hard work from him on the court . He has been true to his word and is becoming a fan favorite. With role players like Williams impressing and superstar guard Luka Doncic on a tear, the Lakers have gotten off to an excellent 15-3 start to the season. Not many expected them to have the best record in the NBA, but it has now been claimed that this is down to an easy schedule. Well, the Lakers will get a chance to make a statement as they take on the 15-4 San Antonio Spurs next at Frost Bank Center on Friday at 9:30 p.m. ET.

The Detroit Lions are facing off against the Chicago Bears on Thanksgiving, and defensive back Brian Branch is going to be key to stopping this high-powered Bears offense. For Branch himself, this week is a huge opportunity to further prove himself in a contract year. Set to hit the open market after 2026, alongside tight end Sam LaPorta, the Lions will have a difficult decision to make with Branch this upcoming offseason. ESPN's Bill Barnwell believes that, instead of a contract extension for Branch, he might be in line for the Lions' franchise tag. Why Brian Branch might be franchise tagged by Lions "With the safety franchise tag projected to come in at $22.2 million, the Lions might see tagging him as a logical way to continue their relationship while they negotiate a long-term extension," Barnwell writes. With the Lions having plenty of offseason questions to solve, once the 2026 season comes to a close, being able to tag Branch and figure things out over an extended period of time would be much easier than trying to work out an extension. Since Branch has had an up-and-down NFL career so far, seeing what Branch can do to close out the 2026 NFL season could give the Lions reason to sign him to a long-term deal. But even if he doesn't finish strong, the Lions could still elect to tag him to avoid letting him hit free agency, where he'd surely get plenty of competitive offers from other teams looking for upgrades. Wisconsin had a disappointing week at the Baha Mar Championship last weekend. Now returning home against Northeastern, the Badgers were notable favorites, with the spread being at 20.5 points ahead of tip-off. But Wisconsin had seen their struggles as big favorites against non-conference teams so far this season. Starting lineup change Wisconsin made two changes in the starting lineup, replacing Eian Elmer with freshman Jackson Ball and Victory Onuetu with Austin Rapp. Ball’s start was short-lived as he suffered a lower-body injury, playing just two minutes on the night. He finished with seven points in 22 minutes, but it still feels like he’s struggling to find his impact on this team. Assertiveness has been a common issue for him so far, but he’s talented enough to find his way. Let’s see if the lineup change sparks that. Bench shows up Without Jack Janicki, the Badgers needed other bench players to show up on Wednesday, and they got that. Hayden Jones provided the spark with 13 points on 5-for-7 shooting, ranking second on the team behind Austin Rapp. He earned praise from Greg Gard after the game for how he responded with his minutes. sports.title: Confirmed: Barcelona star Anthony Gordon named UEFA Champions League Player of the Week
sports.description: Confirmed: Barcelona star Anthony Gordon named UEFA Champions League Player of the Week Following his exploits in the team’s 4-1 win over Sabah, Barcelona winger Anthony Gordon has been named the UEFA Champions League Player of the Week for Matchday 5 of the league phase. Starting on the left flank in the away fixture in Baku on Wednesday night, the England international was the driving force behind the Catalans’ comfortable victory. Indeed, Gordon found the back of the net on two occasions on the night in Azerbaijan, giving the Blaugrana the lead in the 31st minute in the first half before adding another one six minutes into the second period. Apart from scoring two goals, the 25-year-old attacker caused problems to the home team’s defence for most of the game, justifying manager Hansi Flick’s decision to start him on the night. As such, Gordon has now been voted the UEFA Champions League Player of the Week for Matchday 5 in the league phase. The Barcelona summer signing saw off competition from Cucho Hernandez of Real Betis, Antonio Nusa of RB Leipzig, and Real Madrid superstar Kylian Mbappe, who finished second, third, and fourth, respectively. Apart from being named the Player of the Week, Gordon also makes it to the Champions League Team of the Week for Matchday 5. Since arriving at Barcelona in the summer, the 25-year-old has made a solid start , scoring and assisting five goals apiece from 17 matches across all competitions. Involved in a competition for a starting spot on the left flank with Karim Adeyemi, Gordon has been Flick’s preferred option and his performance against Sabah further strengthened his credentials.

technology.title: Tech's outage problem needs maintenance, not conspiracy theories
technology.description: Years of technical debt, increasingly complex systems, and underinvestment in IT operations have left organizations vulnerable to major outages, according to Forrester. The analyst pointed to a seven-day stretch in November when failures disrupted Microsoft 365, US air traffic control, banking, and other critical services. The coinciding outages provoked "a slew of conspiracy theories about cyberattacks and AI," Forrester said. "The real culprit is tragically mundane: the culmination of decades of technical debt, the frenetic buildout of massively complex and highly interdependent systems, the concentration of risk, and the underinvestment in advanced operations." Forrester urged technology suppliers and in-house IT teams to prioritize resilience as their systems grow more complex. Otherwise, "the tech estate will collapse like a house of cards, taking down consumer and business trust with it." Earlier this month, Microsoft was left struggling to restore many of its cloud services after a core process running on some servers became "overwhelmed" and its attempts to fix the problem failed. Some of its services did not recover for another 24 hours. In October, Google Cloud blamed a "power event" for taking down multiple online products for customers in Western Europe. Affected services included BigQuery Data Transfer Service, Cloud Filestore, Cloud Run, Google App Engine, and Google Kubernetes Engine. In October last year , a major outage impacted Amazon Web Services (AWS), with even Amazon's own web page reported to be offline and dozens of other online services and websites affected. Aviation and banking were also hit this month. A communications outage triggered a nationwide ground stop in the US on November 13 , while incidents involving JPMorgan Chase, United Airlines, Apple, Workday, Gmail, and other services added to the sense of widespread instability. "Claims that these were all part of one connected cyberattack or conspiracy are highly unlikely. The real story is much more mundane," the report said . Forrester argued that organizations have prioritized visible improvements over repairs to the underlying technology. "Modernization investments have favored visible change over structural renewal," wrote report authors Lauren Nelson and Mark Moccia. "Organizations routinely fund new customer experiences, cloud migrations, platform consolidation, and AI initiatives because leaders can connect them to growth or productivity. "They are less enthusiastic about updating core systems, simplifying architectures, retiring obsolete components, and eliminating fragile interfaces. The result is a modern front end resting on an aging, brittle, and increasingly interconnected estate." Forrester's recommendations are to map dependencies, test failures and recovery under realistic conditions, and use incidents and near misses to identify weaknesses before they cause another outage. ®

technology.title: UK privacy watchdog faces probe into its workplace culture
technology.description: Britain's privacy watchdog is getting a taste of its own medicine, with an independent review set to examine the culture, governance, and accountability surrounding the events that led to former Information Commissioner John Edwards' resignation. Karon Monaghan KC will examine whether the regulator's culture and governance allowed problems to develop or made concerns harder to raise. Edwards quit in June after an independent workplace investigation found there was a "case to answer" over his behavior and that his conduct fell short of what was expected of a public official. He disagreed with some of its findings, but ultimately conceded that he had shown "poor judgment." That investigation, however, focused on Edwards alone. According to the terms of reference published on Thursday, it "did not consider the wider conditions in which that conduct occurred, and it was not designed to." The new review will cast a wider net. Monaghan wants to know whether staff could call out bad behavior further up the food chain, and what awaited those who tried. It will also poke around the regulator's leadership and governance arrangements and its relationship with its sponsoring government department, including whether there were adequate ways for concerns to be escalated and those at the top to be challenged. Current and former staff can give evidence confidentially and voluntarily, while Monaghan will be given access to relevant documents and existing material, including staff surveys and data on bullying, harassment and discrimination. The ICO has confirmed it won't use confidentiality clauses in settlement agreements to prevent people from contributing to the review. Monaghan decides which witnesses and documents are relevant, rather than the ICO or DCMS. Access remains subject to legal restrictions, and she must be told when material is withheld and why. She can speak to whoever she thinks is relevant and ask for the complaints, correspondence, and other paperwork she needs. And if that leads her somewhere unexpected, she can ask to widen the investigation. DCMS can refuse, but it won't be able to quietly brush the request aside, and any decision not to expand the scope has to make it into the final report. The review won't reopen the investigation into Edwards, make findings about the conduct of named individuals, or delve into the merits of the regulator's enforcement decisions. Its arrival comes amid a broader shake-up at Britain's data watchdog. The old Information Commissioner's Office was formally replaced by the Information Commission on September 30, bringing with it a new board-led governance model. The government first promised the wider review in July, shortly after Edwards' departure, but it didn't appoint its reviewer or nail down the terms until late November. technology.title: 'Significant number of customer records' pwned in Flight Centre Travel Group breach
technology.description: Travel giant Flight Centre Travel Group (FLT) says "a significant number of customer records" may have been accessed by "unknown persons" following a cyberattack. The Brisbane-headquartered company said the incident affected a third-party accommodation booking system used by Flight Centre, Travel Associates, Cruiseabout, and some independent travel agents. Its disclosure [PDF], filed with the Australian Securities Exchange today, added that it was aware that records were accessed, but cannot definitively say how many were exfiltrated. Flight Centre is working with the supplier and incident response specialist Mandiant to establish the scope of the incident. An initial review suggests most accessed records contained only customer names, some with basic travel information. A "very small percentage" may also include birth dates, email addresses, limited passport details, phone numbers, or, in rare cases, health or mobility information. Flight bookings and corporate travel use separate systems and are unaffected, the company said. "FLT values customer privacy and data security," the company said in its disclosure. "The company understands that an incident like this can be unsettling for customers who may be affected, and we apologize for any concern this causes." Investigations remain ongoing, but FLT has already contained the attack, rotated keys and credentials, and increased system monitoring, it said. The company said it would contact affected customers directly. Its brands continue to operate normally, and travelers should proceed with their plans. Customers should independently verify unexpected messages about their bookings before clicking links, opening attachments, or sharing personal information. The attack on FLT follows others that have hit booking systems in the past year, including those on Booking.com and BWH Hotels . More recently, another Australian business, RMS Cloud, which provides booking software to travel and leisure companies, also acknowledged a breach that led to WhatsApp scams in late October. Numerous reports of travelers being targeted with messages that contained their names and booking details hit local news outlets at the time. Customers were sent convincing messages seemingly from the hotels they had booked, and according to Australia's National Anti-Scam Centre, the scams appeared to be financially motivated. Muhammad Yahya Patel, vCISO and cybersecurity advisor for EMEA at Huntress, said attackers targeting booking systems is a "familiar supply chain story" that has a greater impact than simple data theft.
